svg.title: Grade → speed and heart-rate inertia
svg.desc: Two line charts of real Runsketch engine output. Left: running speed relative to flat ground, which falls to 0.74 times flat speed at a 10 per cent climb and peaks at 1.16 times on a 9 per cent descent before turning back down; a shaded band shows descent skill spreading the descent branch from beginner to elite, whose upper edge is Kay's 2012 curve fitted to hill-race records; walking follows Tobler's function, peaking at 1.19 times at 5 per cent down; and a dotted reference shows that holding energy cost constant would mean 2.0 times flat speed at 20 per cent down. Right: when heart-rate demand steps from 120 to 150 bpm, heart rate covers 63 per cent of the step in 50 seconds, and returns through 63 per cent of the fall in 100 seconds if the runner keeps moving but 160 seconds once stopped.
